opening_message:
Ticket 1: Casey Wu (employee ID E005) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E005.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Casey Wu (E005) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted; write is the maximum for this employee. Requested write is within policy, recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Casey Wu (E005) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, the maximum is read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommending read.
reason: The two memory notes conflict on Casey Wu's employment type: HR reports full_time (which would permit write for Source Code, since admin requires the Engineer role), while Security reports contractor with basic security training, for whom write is only permitted with advanced training (maximum = read). Since the requested write cannot be safely verified under the contractor record and over-granting would violate policy, I grant the more conservative maximum of read.
